small_guidance:
- The softmax/sigmoid kernel is already cheap; the conv_transpose3d dominates the 14.4 ms runtime (baseline 5.3 ms means the torch ConvTranspose3d call here is slower than baseline because softmax+sigmoid are also in baseline). Tuning BLOCK_C/num_warps on the elementwise kernel will not move fast_p meaningfully.
- If staying small, at least try `memory_format=torch.channels_last_3d` on the conv output and switch the softmax kernel to load C contiguously (channels-last layout), since C=64 is a clean BLOCK_C with num_warps=2.
- Add `num_stages=2` explicitly and try BLOCK_C=64 fixed (not next_pow2 padded) with num_warps∈{1,2} since each program only reduces 64 elements.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) that computes the input×kernel outer product and scatter-adds into the output grid, handling stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1 in index math. This is the dominant op (~95% of runtime) and torch's ConvTranspose3d is the bottleneck.
- Alternatively, implement as a gather-style direct kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), and for each output voxel iterate over input contributions `(id+pad-kd)/stride` with divisibility check. Fold bias add into the epilogue, then fuse softmax-over-C and sigmoid by tiling output programs along (N, spatial) with BLOCK_C=64 covering all channels, so softmax+sigmoid happen on registers before the store — eliminating the second pass entirely.
- Use channels-last-3d layout (N, D, H, W, C) so the OC axis is contiguous, enabling coalesced GEMM-K loads and a single-pass softmax across C in the same kernel. Autotune tiles (BM,BN,BK) starting at (32,32,16) num_warps=4 num_stages=2 to stay within SMEM.
